result.sourceSentence: Edited for reading; links, citations and media omitted.
result.translation: 为便于阅读而编辑；已省略链接、引文和媒体。

result.sourceSentence: Introduction
result.translation: 引言

result.sourceSentence: Scientific activity has been compared to a scholarly conversation.
result.translation: 科学活动被比作学术对话。

result.sourceSentence: As scientific communities are now very large, this conversation mostly proceeds by writing and reading.
result.translation: 由于科学共同体如今非常庞大，这种对话主要通过写作和阅读来进行。

result.sourceSentence: While lot of advice exists about the writing part, much less attention has been devoted to what to read.
result.translation: 虽然关于写作部分有很多建议，但人们对“该读什么”投入的关注却少得多。

result.sourceSentence: Reading is fundamental for keeping updated in the advances of your discipline.
result.translation: 阅读对于持续跟进本学科的进展至关重要。

result.sourceSentence: However, scholarly literature grows at an increasingly fast pace.
result.translation: 然而，学术文献正以越来越快的速度增长。

result.sourceSentence: Scientists, regardless of the stage in their career, have trouble in navigating an overwhelming amount of relevant literature.
result.translation: 科学家无论处于职业生涯的哪个阶段，在梳理海量相关文献时都会遇到困难。

result.sourceSentence: This overload can potentially lead to increasingly selective or cursory reading.
result.translation: 这种过载可能会导致阅读越来越有选择性或粗略。

result.sourceSentence: Consequences are detrimental for the training of new scientists by decreasing quality standards.
result.translation: 其后果会通过降低质量标准而有损新科学家的培养。

result.sourceSentence: Good reading habits are essential and need to be instilled from the very beginning of a scientific career.
result.translation: 良好的阅读习惯至关重要，需要从科研生涯的最开始就加以培养。

result.sourceSentence: As a coordinator of a doctoral program, I have addressed this issue in a recent workshop, after realizing the demand of advice on this topic by many graduate students.
result.translation: 作为博士项目的协调人，在意识到许多研究生对这一主题有建议需求后，我在近期的一次研讨会上探讨了这个问题。

result.sourceSentence: Here, I summarize the content of this workshop in 10 simple rules for achieving good reading habits.
result.translation: 在此，我将这次研讨会的内容总结为 10 条简单规则，以养成良好的阅读习惯。

result.sourceSentence: They were mainly intended to guide early graduate students, but I believe they can also be useful at later career stages.
result.translation: 它们主要用于指导低年级研究生，但我相信它们在后期的职业阶段也有用。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 1: Develop the habit of reading on a daily basis
result.translation: 规则 1：养成每天阅读的习惯

result.sourceSentence: A first step toward good reading habits is to realize that reading is a fundamental part of your training (or activity) as a researcher.
result.translation: 迈向良好阅读习惯的第一步，是认识到阅读是你作为研究者所受训练（或活动）的基础部分。

result.sourceSentence: If you do not read regularly, you will soon get out of date and will not be able to join the scholarly conversation.
result.translation: 如果你没有定期阅读，很快就会落伍，也无法加入学术对话。

result.sourceSentence: Piling or archiving unread papers (see Rule 9) only leads to a delusion of knowledge.
result.translation: 堆积或归档未读论文（参见规则 9）只会带来拥有知识的错觉。

result.sourceSentence: Cursory or urgent reading when preparing a new article is neither efficient nor desirable.
result.translation: 在准备新文章时粗略或仓促地阅读，既不高效，也不可取。

result.sourceSentence: Instead, dedicate daily time slot for reading at least one paper.
result.translation: 相反，每天专门留出时间段来阅读至少一篇论文。

result.sourceSentence: When to read is a very personal decision.
result.translation: 何时阅读是一个非常个人化的决定。

result.sourceSentence: I use my daily commuting time in public transport for that task; others start their working day doing some reading.
result.translation: 我利用每天乘坐公共交通的通勤时间来完成这项任务；另一些人则通过阅读来开启工作日。

result.sourceSentence: You may find a particularly quiet moment in the day, either at work or at home.
result.translation: 你可能会在一天中找到一个格外安静的时刻，无论是在工作时还是在家里。

result.sourceSentence: If you can only devote short time slots during the day and need several sessions to go through a paper, keeping a routine of daily reading is still advisable; find this time!
result.translation: 如果你在一天中只能投入简短的时段，并且需要分好几次才能读完一篇论文，保持每日阅读的习惯仍然值得推荐；留出这段时间！

result.sourceSentence: Rule 2: Read thoroughly to build a sound background understanding of your topic
result.translation: 规则 2：深入阅读，对你的主题建立扎实的背景理解

result.sourceSentence: Particularly at early career stages, you need to get as much background information as possible.
result.translation: 尤其是在职业早期阶段，你需要尽可能多地获取背景信息。

result.sourceSentence: If you think you are short of time during your graduate period, just imagine how busy you will be later when you teach, supervise students, manage research projects; do not take shortcuts!
result.translation: 如果你觉得在研究生阶段时间不够，试想一下以后当你教学、指导学生、管理研究项目时会有多忙；不要走捷径！

result.sourceSentence: Reading articles thoroughly will provide you a broad context about concepts, methods, results, and potential meanings and implications in your discipline.
result.translation: 深入阅读文章将为你提供你所在学科中关于概念、方法、结果以及潜在含义和影响的广泛背景。

result.sourceSentence: Once you have achieved a good background knowledge of a topic, you can start reading more selectively those papers or paper sections that fill a particular gap or curiosity.
result.translation: 一旦你对某个主题获得了良好的背景知识，就可以开始更有选择性地阅读那些填补特定空白或满足好奇心的论文或论文章节。

result.sourceSentence: But a good background knowledge takes a long time to build; do your homework early in your career so that you can save time later.
result.translation: 但扎实的背景知识需要很长时间来积累；在职业生涯早期做好功课，这样日后就能节省时间。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 3: Do not ignore the pillars of your discipline; read the classics
result.translation: 规则 3：不要忽视你所在学科的支柱；阅读经典著作

result.sourceSentence: I repeat, read the classics!
result.translation: 我重申，阅读经典著作！

result.sourceSentence: You may be working at the cutting edge of science, but your discipline surely has a long history behind it.
result.translation: 你可能正在科学前沿工作，但你的学科背后必定有着悠久的历史。

result.sourceSentence: It is naïve to think that you can go on in science by reading only what is new, starting at the moment you got involved in science, and ignore past fundamental steps in the building of your discipline (even if obsolete for current standards!).
result.translation: 以为从你涉足科学的那一刻起，只读最新内容就能在科学道路上走下去，而忽视学科建设中过往的奠基性阶段（即便按当前标准已然过时！），这种想法未免太天真了。

result.sourceSentence: You need to identify and read the foundational papers of your discipline, concerning concepts, methods, or views.
result.translation: 你需要找出并阅读你所在学科中关于概念、方法或观点的奠基性论文。

result.sourceSentence: If this brings you back two centuries, so be it!
result.translation: 如果这会把你带回两个世纪前，那就这样吧！

result.sourceSentence: Only by reading the classics you will get a deep understanding of your research topic.
result.translation: 只有阅读经典著作，你才能对自己的研究课题有深刻的理解。

result.sourceSentence: This will not only prevent you from reinventing the wheel but will enable you to build a robust context for significant advances.
result.translation: 这不仅能避免你重复造轮子，还能使你为重大进展构建扎实的背景。

result.sourceSentence: Repeat, read the classics!
result.translation: 重申一遍，阅读经典著作！

result.sourceSentence: Rule 4: If you have to get familiar with a new topic, consider reading in chronological order
result.translation: 规则 4：如果你需要熟悉一个新课题，可以考虑按时间顺序阅读

result.sourceSentence: Early in your career, or whenever you get into a new topic and gather a bunch of references to get a hint on the status of the field, consider reading them in chronological order.
result.translation: 在职业生涯初期，或者每当你涉足一个新课题并收集一批参考文献以初步了解该领域的现状时，不妨考虑按时间顺序阅读这些文献。

result.sourceSentence: If all references are recent, this gives you an idea of how the conversation is developing and who is answering who.
result.translation: 如果所有参考文献都是近期的，这能让你了解讨论是如何发展的，以及谁在回应谁。

result.sourceSentence: If the time lapse is longer, you will get surprised to discover how concepts, methods, or interpretations may have changed with time.
result.translation: 如果时间跨度更长，你会惊讶地发现，概念、方法或解释可能随时间推移发生了怎样的变化。

result.sourceSentence: Reading in chronological order will allow you to realize subtle—or dramatic—changes in term use or meaning that will profitably add to your background knowledge of the topic.
result.translation: 按时间顺序阅读能让你察觉到术语用法或含义上的细微——或剧烈——变化，这会大有裨益地增进你对该主题的背景知识。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 5: Avoid narrow-mindedness by reading beyond your discipline
result.translation: 规则 5：通过阅读自身学科之外的内容，避免思想狭隘

result.sourceSentence: Interesting ideas, concepts, methods, or implications are waiting for you in the work of other disciplines.
result.translation: 在其他学科的成果中，有趣的想法、概念、方法或启示正等待着你。

result.sourceSentence: Keep an eye to advances in other fields.
result.translation: 留意其他领域的进展。

result.sourceSentence: You do not need to become the next Leonardo da Vinci; find a balance between focused and broad reading.
result.translation: 你不必成为下一个列奥纳多·达·芬奇；要在专注与广泛的阅读之间找到平衡。

result.sourceSentence: The trick is to identify a few journals with a broad scope or that provide reviews in a broad spectrum of topics within a larger field and browse their content regularly (see Rule 6).
result.translation: 诀窍在于找出几本涵盖面广，或在较大领域内提供广泛主题综述的期刊，并定期浏览其内容（见规则 6）。

result.sourceSentence: You may also join journal clubs or follow renowned scientists outside your specific field using social networks.
result.translation: 你也可以加入期刊俱乐部，或利用社交网络关注你特定领域之外的知名科学家。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 6: Create a list of relevant journals
result.translation: 规则 6：创建相关期刊列表

result.sourceSentence: Find out which journals publish relevant information for your research and subscribe to the online alerts for new content.
result.translation: 找出哪些期刊会发表与你的研究相关的信息，并订阅新内容的在线提醒。

result.sourceSentence: Think big; if you find yourself checking less than 20 journals, you are probably missing relevant sources.
result.translation: 往大处想；如果你发现自己查阅的期刊少于 20 种，你可能遗漏了相关来源。

result.sourceSentence: Include journals that only occasionally publish relevant information.
result.translation: 将仅偶尔发表相关信息的期刊也纳入其中。

result.sourceSentence: Do not forget those journals in which new analytical, experimental, or statistical methods are published, as they not always overlap with the journals in which primary research is published.
result.translation: 不要忘记那些发表新的分析、实验或统计方法的期刊，因为它们并不总是与发表原始研究的期刊重合。

result.sourceSentence: Be prepared to reassess your list of journals during your scientific career; journals bust and fade and editorial lines change.
result.translation: 在你的科研生涯中，要准备好重新评估你的期刊列表；期刊会倒闭消亡，编辑方针也会改变。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 7: Not all interesting stuff will appear in articles; read books
result.translation: 规则 7：并非所有有趣的内容都会出现在文章中；要阅读书籍

result.sourceSentence: Books distil accumulated knowledge or suggest groundbreaking ideas.
result.translation: 书籍浓缩了积累的知识，或提出开创性的想法。

result.sourceSentence: Read books, both classic and recent.
result.translation: 阅读书籍，无论是经典的还是近期的。

result.sourceSentence: Spotting the classic books is relatively easy and, with luck, you may be allowed to “plunder” the library of the elders around (Rule 10).
result.translation: 发现经典书籍相对容易；如果运气好，你或许会被允许“洗劫”周围前辈的藏书（规则 10）。

result.sourceSentence: However, finding new relevant books is not as straightforward as finding new articles.
result.translation: 然而，找到相关的新书不像查找新文章那样直接。

result.sourceSentence: Google Scholar and most of the big editorials offer alerts or mailing lists for new books that can be customized.
result.translation: 谷歌学术和大多数大型出版社都提供可自定义的新书提醒或邮件列表。

result.sourceSentence: Another possibility is to identify the journals that include regular sections on new books, such as Quarterly Review of Biology.
result.translation: 另一种方法是找出设有新书固定栏目的期刊，例如《生物学季刊》。

result.sourceSentence: Finally, check with the library of your institution how new books are advertised—probably as electronic alerts—as the traditional shelf with novelties is almost extinct.
result.translation: 最后，向你所在机构的图书馆咨询新书是如何发布的——很可能是以电子提醒的形式——因为摆放新书的传统书架已几乎绝迹。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 8: Use a reference manager to keep track of your literature
result.translation: 规则8：使用文献管理工具来追踪你的文献

result.sourceSentence: Reference managers will avoid chaotic accumulation of nonretrievable literature.
result.translation: 文献管理工具可以避免无法检索的文献混乱堆积。

result.sourceSentence: Some discipline is required to avoid misuse of reference managers.
result.translation: 需要一定的自律来避免误用文献管理工具。

result.sourceSentence: First, devote some time every day to update your recent readings.
result.translation: 首先，每天抽出一些时间来更新你近期的阅读记录。

result.sourceSentence: Second, never store in your reference manager papers you have not read; scientific databases already do that for you.
result.translation: 其次，切勿将你尚未阅读的论文存入文献管理工具中；科学数据库已经为你做好了这件事。

result.sourceSentence: Unread papers are best filed in a “to read” folder, that can be subdivided according to topics or urgency.
result.translation: 未读论文最好归档在“待读”文件夹中，该文件夹可以根据主题或紧急程度细分。

result.sourceSentence: Third, remember that storing a paper in a reference manager forces you to identify meaningful key words.
result.translation: 第三，记住，将论文存入文献管理工具会迫使你确定有意义的关键词。

result.sourceSentence: Thus, refrain from merely importing key words already included in the reference and create your personalized list of keywords because this will contribute to building your background knowledge of the discipline.
result.translation: 因此，避免仅仅导入参考文献中已包含的关键词，而应创建你个性化的关键词列表，因为这有助于建立你对该学科的背景知识。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 9: Keep a long-term review for your own use as a way to remember what you read
result.translation: 规则9：保留一份供自己使用的长期综述，作为记住阅读内容的方法

result.sourceSentence: The more you read, the more you forget!
result.translation: 读得越多，忘得越多！

result.sourceSentence: A fruitful way to remember what you read is to open one (or several) review(s) of a topic for your own use.
result.translation: 记住阅读内容的有效方法，就是针对某个主题建立一份（或几份）供自己使用的综述。

result.sourceSentence: You may use your reference manager to do that (Rule 8).
result.translation: 你可以使用文献管理软件来做这件事（规则8）。

result.sourceSentence: Nevertheless, I recommend going a step further and have a spreadsheet or a text document to store basic information or main messages from the primary literature.
result.translation: 不过，我建议更进一步，准备一个电子表格或文本文档来保存原始文献中的基本信息或主要观点。

result.sourceSentence: Whatever the format you choose, this review will allow you to retrieve much more easily confirmatory or negative evidence that you might use when writing an introduction or a discussion.
result.translation: 无论你选择哪种格式，这份综述都能让你更加容易地检索到在撰写引言或讨论时可能用到的支持性或反面证据。

result.sourceSentence: At the same time, it will serve as a “note to yourself” for future surveys in the topic.
result.translation: 同时，它也将作为日后对该主题进行综述时的“备忘录”。

result.sourceSentence: Of course, it can eventually lead to a formal review paper.
result.translation: 当然，它最终可能会促成一篇正式的综述论文。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 10: Build your own library to make yourself independent and inspire others
result.translation: 规则 10：建立自己的文献库，让自己独立并启发他人

result.sourceSentence: As soon as you can, start your own collection of papers and books.
result.translation: 尽可能早地开始建立自己的论文和书籍收藏。

result.sourceSentence: Do not rely exclusively on your supervisor’s (or your colleagues’ or your institution’s) library.
result.translation: 不要仅仅依赖导师（或同事、或所在机构）的图书馆。

result.sourceSentence: Certainly, the internet is there to store the information for you …except when it is not!
result.translation: 诚然，互联网就在那里为你存储信息……除了它不在的时候！

result.sourceSentence: The same applies to the library of your institution, particularly outside the top scientific countries where research funding is haphazard.
result.translation: 同样的情况也适用于你所在机构的图书馆，尤其是在顶尖科学国家之外，那里的研究经费毫无规律。

result.sourceSentence: Consider subscribing to some particularly interesting journal or becoming a member of a society that publishes a relevant journal.
result.translation: 考虑订阅一些特别有趣的期刊，或成为出版相关期刊的学会成员。

result.sourceSentence: Building your own library in paper might be challenging early in your career due to funding limitations or movement between institutions during your postdoc stage.
result.translation: 在职业生涯早期，由于经费限制或博士后阶段在各机构间流动，建立自己的纸质藏书可能会充满挑战。

result.sourceSentence: Nevertheless, applying this rule should not wait until you get a permanent position, and a digital library is always an option.
result.translation: 尽管如此，应用这条规则不应等到获得永久职位之后，而且数字图书馆始终是一个选择。

result.sourceSentence: For scientists at later stages in their career, a personal library should be considered a must, as an important part of mentoring.
result.translation: 对于处于职业生涯后期阶段的科学家而言，个人藏书应被视为必备之物，作为指导工作的重要组成部分。

result.sourceSentence: I might be a little old-fashioned, but for those of us who grew intellectually surrounded by books and journals in our departmental library—and plundered others’ libraries—the mere presence of books around creates an inspiring atmosphere.
result.translation: 我可能有点老派，但对我们这些被院系图书馆的书籍和期刊环绕、并在智识上成长——还“搜刮”过他人藏书——的人来说，仅仅是身边有书籍存在，就能营造出一种鼓舞人心的氛围。

result.sourceSentence: Provide the same atmosphere for your fellow students or colleagues.
result.translation: 为你的同学或同事提供同样的氛围。

result.sourceSentence: License: CC BY 4.0.
result.translation: 许可协议：CC BY 4.0。

result.sourceSentence: Edited for reading; links, citations and media omitted.
result.translation: 为便于阅读而编辑；已省略链接、引文和媒体。

result.sourceSentence: Introduction
result.translation: 引言

result.sourceSentence: “There is no problem that a library card can’t solve” according to author Eleanor Brown.
result.translation: 据作家埃莉诺·布朗所说：“没有什么问题是借书证解决不了的。”

result.sourceSentence: This advice is sound, probably for both life and science, but even the best tool (like the library) is most effective when accompanied by instructions and a basic understanding of how and when to use it.
result.translation: 这一建议对生活和科学大概都有道理，但即便是最好的工具（比如图书馆），也只有在辅以使用说明以及对如何、何时使用它的基本理解时，才最为有效。

result.sourceSentence: For many budding scientists, the first day in a new lab setting often involves a stack of papers, an email full of links to pertinent articles, or some promise of a richer understanding so long as one reads enough of the scientific literature.
result.translation: 对许多初出茅庐的科学家而言，在新实验室环境中的第一天，往往意味着一摞论文、一封满是相关文章链接的电子邮件，或某种承诺——只要阅读足够多的科学文献，就能获得更深入的理解。

result.sourceSentence: However, the purpose and approach to reading a scientific article is unlike that of reading a news story, novel, or even a textbook and can initially seem unapproachable.
result.translation: 然而，阅读科学文章的目的和方法不同于阅读新闻报道、小说甚至教科书，起初可能会显得难以亲近。

result.sourceSentence: Having good habits for reading scientific literature is key to setting oneself up for success, identifying new research questions, and filling in the gaps in one’s current understanding; developing these good habits is the first crucial step.
result.translation: 养成阅读科学文献的良好习惯，是为成功奠定基础、发现新研究问题以及填补当前理解中的空白的关键；培养这些良好习惯是至关重要的第一步。

result.sourceSentence: Advice typically centers around two main tips: read actively and read often.
result.translation: 建议通常围绕两个主要技巧展开：主动阅读和经常阅读。

result.sourceSentence: However, active reading, or reading with an intent to understand, is both a learned skill and a level of effort.
result.translation: 然而，主动阅读，即带着理解意图去阅读，既是一项习得的技能，也体现了努力的程度。

result.sourceSentence: Although there is no one best way to do this, we present 10 simple rules, relevant to novices and seasoned scientists alike, to teach our strategy for active reading based on our experience as readers and as mentors of undergraduate and graduate researchers, medical students, fellows, and early career faculty.
result.translation: 尽管没有唯一最佳的方法来做到这一点，我们还是提出了 10 条对新手和资深科学家同样适用的简单规则，基于我们作为阅读者以及作为本科生和研究生科研人员、医学生、研究员与职业生涯早期教职人员导师的经验，来传授我们的主动阅读策略。

result.sourceSentence: Rules 1–5 are big picture recommendations.
result.translation: 规则 1–5 是宏观层面的建议。

result.sourceSentence: Rules 6–8 relate to philosophy of reading.
result.translation: 规则 6–8 涉及阅读理念。

result.sourceSentence: Rules 9–10 guide the “now what?”
result.translation: 规则 9–10 指导“接下来怎么办？”

result.sourceSentence: questions one should ask after reading and how to integrate what was learned into one’s own science.
result.translation: 阅读后应当提出的问题，以及如何将所学内容融入自己的科学研究。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 1: Pick your reading goal
result.translation: 规则 1：选择你的阅读目标

result.sourceSentence: What you want to get out of an article should influence your approach to reading it. includes a handful of example intentions and how you might prioritize different parts of the same article differently based on your goals as a reader.
result.translation: 你想从一篇文章中获得什么，应该会影响你阅读它的方式。其中包含几个意图示例，以及你可以如何根据自己作为读者的目标，以不同方式优先处理同一篇文章的不同部分。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 2: Understand the author’s goal
result.translation: 规则 2：理解作者的目标

result.sourceSentence: In written communication, the reader and the writer are equally important.
result.translation: 在书面交流中，读者和作者同样重要。

result.sourceSentence: Both influence the final outcome: in this case, your scientific understanding!
result.translation: 两者都会影响最终结果：在这种情况下，就是你的科学理解！

result.sourceSentence: After identifying your goal, think about the author’s goal for sharing this project.
result.translation: 在明确你的目标之后，思考作者分享这个项目的目标。

result.sourceSentence: This will help you interpret the data and understand the author’s interpretation of the data.
result.translation: 这将帮助你解读数据，并理解作者对数据的解读。

result.sourceSentence: However, this requires some understanding of who the author(s) are (e.g., what are their scientific interests?), the scientific field in which they work (e.g., what techniques are available in this field?), and how this paper fits into the author’s research (e.g., is this work building on an author’s longstanding project or controversial idea?).
result.translation: 然而，这需要一定程度上了解作者是谁（例如，他们的科学兴趣是什么？）、他们所从事的科学领域（例如，该领域有哪些可用技术？），以及这篇论文如何融入作者的研究（例如，这项工作是否建立在作者长期进行的项目或有争议的观点之上？）。

result.sourceSentence: This information may be hard to glean without experience and a history of reading.
result.translation: 如果缺乏经验和阅读积累，这些信息可能很难获取。

result.sourceSentence: But don’t let this be a discouragement to starting the process; it is by the act of reading that this experience is gained!
result.translation: 但不要让这成为开始这一过程的阻碍；正是通过阅读这一行为，这种经验才得以获得！

result.sourceSentence: A good step toward understanding the goal of the author(s) is to ask yourself: What kind of article is this?
result.translation: 要理解作者的目标，一个很好的做法是问问自己：这是一篇什么类型的文章？

result.sourceSentence: Journals publish different types of articles, including methods, review, commentary, resources, and research articles as well as other types that are specific to a particular journal or groups of journals.
result.translation: 期刊会发表不同类型的文章，包括方法、综述、评论、资源和研究文章，以及某本特定期刊或期刊组特有的其他类型。

result.sourceSentence: These article types have different formatting requirements and expectations for content.
result.translation: 这些文章类型有不同的格式要求和内容预期。

result.sourceSentence: Knowing the article type will help guide your evaluation of the information presented.
result.translation: 了解文章类型将有助于指导你评估所呈现的信息。

result.sourceSentence: Is the article a methods paper, presenting a new technique?
result.translation: 这篇文章是一篇介绍新技术的方法论文吗？

result.sourceSentence: Is the article a review article, intended to summarize a field or problem?
result.translation: 这篇文章是旨在总结某一领域或问题的综述文章吗？

result.sourceSentence: Is it a commentary, intended to take a stand on a controversy or give a big picture perspective on a problem?
result.translation: 它是一篇旨在对某一争议表明立场，或对某一问题给出宏观视角的评论吗？

result.sourceSentence: Is it a resource article, presenting a new tool or data set for others to use?
result.translation: 它是一篇介绍供他人使用的新工具或数据集的资源文章吗？

result.sourceSentence: Is it a research article, written to present new data and the authors’ interpretation of those data?
result.translation: 它是一篇为呈现新数据及作者对这些数据的解释而撰写的研究文章吗？

result.sourceSentence: The type of paper, and its intended purpose, will get you on your way to understanding the author’s goal.
result.translation: 论文的类型及其预期目的，将让你开始理解作者的目标。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 3: Ask six questions
result.translation: 规则 3：提出六个问题

result.sourceSentence: When reading, ask yourself: (1) What do the author(s) want to know (motivation)?
result.translation: 阅读时，问问自己：(1) 作者想知道什么（动机）？

result.sourceSentence: (2) What did they do (approach/methods)?
result.translation: （2）他们做了什么（思路/方法）？

result.sourceSentence: (3) Why was it done that way (context within the field)?
result.translation: （3）为什么要那样做（该领域内的背景）？

result.sourceSentence: (4) What do the results show?
result.translation: （4）结果显示了什么？

result.sourceSentence: (5) How did the author(s) interpret the results (interpretation/discussion)?
result.translation: （5）作者是如何解读结果的（解读/讨论）？

result.sourceSentence: (6) What should be done next?
result.translation: （6）接下来应该做什么？

result.sourceSentence: (Regarding this last question, the author(s) may provide some suggestions in the discussion, but the key is to ask yourself what you think should come next.)
result.translation: （关于最后一个问题，作者可能会在讨论中提供一些建议，但关键是要问问自己，你认为接下来应该做什么。）

result.sourceSentence: Each of these questions can and should be asked about the complete work as well as each table, figure, or experiment within the paper.
result.translation: 这些问题中的每一个都可以且应该针对整项工作，以及论文中的每张表格、插图或实验来提出。

result.sourceSentence: Early on, it can take a long time to read one article front to back, and this can be intimidating.
result.translation: 起初，从头到尾阅读一篇文章可能会花费很长时间，这可能会让人望而生畏。

result.sourceSentence: Break down your understanding of each section of the work with these questions to make the effort more manageable.
result.translation: 借助这些问题分解你对文章每个部分的理解，让这项工作更易于掌控。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 4: Unpack each figure and table
result.translation: 规则 4：剖析每张图和表

result.sourceSentence: Scientists write original research papers primarily to present new data that may change or reinforce the collective knowledge of a field.
result.translation: 科学家撰写原创研究论文，主要是为了呈现新数据，这些数据可能会改变或巩固某一领域的集体知识。

result.sourceSentence: Therefore, the most important parts of this type of scientific paper are the data.
result.translation: 因此，这类科学论文中最重要的部分就是数据。

result.sourceSentence: Some people like to scrutinize the figures and tables (including legends) before reading any of the “main text”: because all of the important information should be obtained through the data.
result.translation: 有些人喜欢在阅读任何“正文”之前仔细审视图和表（包括图例），因为所有重要信息都应该通过数据获取。

result.sourceSentence: Others prefer to read through the results section while sequentially examining the figures and tables as they are addressed in the text.
result.translation: 另一些人更倾向于通读结果部分，同时随着图和表在正文中被提及而依次查看。

result.sourceSentence: There is no correct or incorrect approach: Try both to see what works best for you.
result.translation: 没有正确或错误的方法：两种都试试，看看哪种最适合你。

result.sourceSentence: The key is making sure that one understands the presented data and how it was obtained.
result.translation: 关键在于确保理解所呈现的数据以及它是如何获取的。

result.sourceSentence: For each figure, work to understand each x- and y-axes, color scheme, statistical approach (if one was used), and why the particular plotting approach was used.
result.translation: 对于每张图，努力理解每个 x 轴和 y 轴、配色方案、统计方法（如果有使用），以及为什么采用这种特定的绘图方法。

result.sourceSentence: For each table, identify what experimental groups and variables are presented.
result.translation: 对于每个表格，找出呈现了哪些实验组和变量。

result.sourceSentence: Identify what is shown and how the data were collected.
result.translation: 找出展示了什么内容，以及数据是如何收集的。

result.sourceSentence: This is typically summarized in the legend or caption but often requires digging deeper into the methods: Do not be afraid to refer back to the methods section frequently to ensure a full understanding of how the presented data were obtained.
result.translation: 这通常在图例或说明中有所概括，但往往需要深入探究方法：不要害怕频繁回看方法部分，以确保充分理解所呈现的数据是如何获取的。

result.sourceSentence: Again, ask the questions in Rule 3 for each figure or panel and conclude with articulating the “take home” message.
result.translation: 再次对每张图或子图提出规则 3 中的问题，最后总结并阐明“核心要点”信息。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 5: Understand the formatting intentions
result.translation: 规则 5：理解格式意图

result.sourceSentence: Just like the overall intent of the article (discussed in Rule 2), the intent of each section within a research article can guide your interpretation.
result.translation: 正如文章的整体意图（在规则 2 中讨论过）一样，研究论文中每个部分的意图都可以指导你的解读。

result.sourceSentence: Some sections are intended to be written as objective descriptions of the data (i.e., the Results section), whereas other sections are intended to present the author’s interpretation of the data.
result.translation: 有些部分旨在写成对数据的客观描述（即“结果”部分），而另一些部分则旨在呈现作者对数据的解读。

result.sourceSentence: Remember though that even “objective” sections are written by and, therefore, influenced by the authors interpretations.
result.translation: 不过请记住，即使是“客观”部分，也是由作者撰写并因此受到作者解读的影响。

result.sourceSentence: Check out to understand the intent of each section of a research article.
result.translation: 查看以了解研究论文中每个部分的意图。

result.sourceSentence: When reading a specific paper, you can also refer to the journal’s website to understand the formatting intentions.
result.translation: 在阅读特定论文时，你也可以查阅该期刊的网站以了解格式意图。

result.sourceSentence: The “For Authors” section of a website will have some nitty gritty information that is less relevant for the reader (like word counts) but will also summarize what the journal editors expect in each section.
result.translation: 网站的“作者须知”部分会有一些对读者来说不太相关的琐碎信息（例如字数统计），但也会概括期刊编辑对每个部分的期望。

result.sourceSentence: This will help to familiarize you with the goal of each article section.
result.translation: 这将有助于你熟悉文章每个部分的目标。

result.sourceSentence: Rule 6: Be critical
result.translation: 规则 6：保持批判性

result.sourceSentence: Published papers are not truths etched in stone.
result.translation: 已发表的论文并非一成不变的真理。

result.sourceSentence: Published papers in high impact journals are not truths etched in stone.
result.translation: 高影响力期刊上已发表的论文并非一成不变的真理。

result.sourceSentence: Published papers by bigwigs in the field are not truths etched in stone.
result.translation: 该领域大人物已发表的论文并非一成不变的真理。

result.sourceSentence: Published papers that seem to agree with your own hypothesis or data are not etched in stone.
result.translation: 看似符合你自己的假设或数据的已发表论文并非一成不变。

result.sourceSentence: Published papers that seem to refute your hypothesis or data are not etched in stone.
result.translation: 看似反驳你的假设或数据的已发表论文并非一成不变。

result.sourceSentence: Science is a never-ending work in progress, and it is essential that the reader pushes back against the author’s interpretation to test the strength of their conclusions.
result.translation: 科学是一项永无止境、不断推进的事业，读者质疑作者的解读至关重要，以此检验其结论的说服力。

result.sourceSentence: Everyone has their own perspective and may interpret the same data in different ways.
result.translation: 每个人都有自己的视角，可能会以不同的方式解读相同的数据。

result.sourceSentence: Mistakes are sometimes published, but more often these apparent errors are due to other factors such as limitations of a methodology and other limits to generalizability (selection bias, unaddressed, or unappreciated confounders).
result.translation: 错误有时会被发表，但更常见的是，这些表面上的错误是由其他因素造成的，例如方法论的局限性以及对普适性的其他限制（选择偏倚、未解决或未察觉的混杂因素）。

result.sourceSentence: When reading a paper, it is important to consider if these factors are pertinent.
result.translation: 阅读论文时，考虑这些因素是否相关很重要。

result.sourceSentence: Critical thinking is a tough skill to learn but ultimately boils down to evaluating data while minimizing biases.
result.translation: 批判性思维是一项很难学会的技能，但最终归结为在评估数据的同时尽量减少偏见。

result.sourceSentence: Ask yourself: Are there other, equally likely, explanations for what is observed?
result.translation: 问问自己：对于观察到的现象，是否还有其他同样可能的解释？

result.sourceSentence: In addition to paying close attention to potential biases of the study or author(s), a reader should also be alert to one’s own preceding perspective (and biases).
result.translation: 除了密切关注研究或作者的潜在偏见外，读者还应当警惕自己原有的视角（以及偏见）。

result.sourceSentence: Take time to ask oneself: Do I find this paper compelling because it affirms something I already think (or wish) is true?
result.translation: 花时间问问自己：我觉得这篇论文有说服力，是因为它印证了我早已认为（或希望）是真的事吗？

result.sourceSentence: Or am I discounting their findings because it differs from what I expect or from my own work?
result.translation: 还是说，我轻视他们的发现，是因为它与我预期的或我自己的研究不同？

result.sourceSentence: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) emphasises the role of biodiversity in delivering benefits essential for all people and, as a result, seeks to safeguard all life-forms.
result.translation: 《生物多样性公约》（CBD）强调生物多样性在为所有人提供不可或缺的益处方面所起的作用，并因此致力于保护所有生命形式。

result.sourceSentence: The indices that are used to measure progress towards international conservation and sustainability goals, however, focus solely on the ‘native’ component of biodiversity.
result.translation: 然而，用于衡量实现国际保护与可持续性目标进展的指数，却仅仅关注生物多样性的“本土”组成部分。

result.sourceSentence: A subset of non-native species can cause undesirable economic, social, or biological effects.
result.translation: 一部分非本土物种可能造成不良的经济、社会或生物影响。

result.sourceSentence: But non-native species also contribute to regional biodiversity (species richness and biotic interactions) and ecosystem services.
result.translation: 但非本土物种也为区域生物多样性（物种丰富度和生物相互作用）及生态系统服务作出贡献。

result.sourceSentence: In some regions and cities, non-native species make up more than half of all species.
result.translation: 在一些地区和城市，非本土物种占所有物种的一半以上。

result.sourceSentence: Currently, the contributions of these species to biodiversity and ecosystem services are overlooked.
result.translation: 目前，这些物种对生物多样性和生态系统服务的贡献被忽视了。

result.sourceSentence: Here, I argue that biodiversity and sustainability indices should include all species.
result.translation: 在此，我主张生物多样性和可持续性指数应当纳入所有物种。

result.sourceSentence: This is not only consistent with definitions of biodiversity but also will promote the idea that long-term, sustainable, human well-being is intricately tied to benefits derived from nature.
result.translation: 这不仅符合生物多样性的定义，还将推动这样一种理念：长期、可持续的人类福祉与源自自然的益处紧密相连。

result.sourceSentence: Humans have a long history of protecting certain elements of nature.
result.translation: 人类有着保护自然界某些要素的悠久历史。

result.sourceSentence: The concepts and values underlying conservation initiatives, however, have changed repeatedly.
result.translation: 然而，支撑保护举措的理念和价值观已多次改变。

result.sourceSentence: Conservation efforts in the 20th century focused primarily on preserving landscapes free of human influence and on preventing the erosion of biodiversity, with an emphasis on protecting rare species from extinction.
result.translation: 20世纪的保护工作主要侧重于保存不受人类影响的景观，以及防止生物多样性受损，并着重保护珍稀物种免于灭绝。

result.sourceSentence: The last 20 years have seen the emergence of additional concepts that emphasise the resilience of nature and the ‘services’ that nature contributes to human well-being.
result.translation: 过去20年见证了更多理念的出现，强调自然的韧性以及自然为人类福祉所贡献的“服务”。

result.sourceSentence: These novel approaches are promoted by some conservation leaders under the assumption that they will broaden the social support for conservation goals.
result.translation: 一些保护界领袖基于以下假设推广这些新颖的方法：它们将扩大社会对保护目标的支持。

result.sourceSentence: The advent of more socially inclusive approaches to conservation biology raises interesting and profound questions regarding the dimensions of the living world we seek to preserve and the political process that is used to specify appropriate conservation objectives.
result.translation: 更具社会包容性的保护生物学方法的出现，引发了有趣而深刻的问题，涉及我们力求保护的生命世界的维度，以及用于明确恰当保护目标的政治进程。

result.sourceSentence: Non-native species, and how they are valued, are at the heart of these ongoing debates.
result.translation: 非本地物种以及人们如何评价它们，正处于这些持续争论的核心。

result.sourceSentence: For the last several decades, non-native species have been portrayed by scientists primarily as a threat to society because a subset can cause economic harm, human-health issues, or the loss of native biodiversity.
result.translation: 近几十年来，科学家主要将非本地物种描绘成对社会的威胁，因为其中一部分物种会造成经济损失、人类健康问题或本地生物多样性的丧失。

result.sourceSentence: The view that non-native species are potentially undesirable persists in indicators used to track progress towards targets of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), where they only appear as a numerical predictor for future invasion events (Aichi Target 9).
result.translation: 认为非本地物种可能不受欢迎的观点，在用于追踪《生物多样性公约》（CBD）目标进展的指标中依然存在；在这些指标里，它们仅作为未来入侵事件的数值预测因子出现（爱知目标9）。

result.sourceSentence: More recently, scientists have also documented the potential positive contributions of non-native species to regional species richness, conservation goals, and to the ecosystem services they contribute to certain stakeholders within society.
result.translation: 近年来，科学家也记录了非本地物种对区域物种丰富度、保护目标，以及其为社会中特定利益相关方提供的生态系统服务所作出的潜在积极贡献。

result.sourceSentence: In some instances, non-native species are rapidly appreciated for their cultural ecosystem services.
result.translation: 在某些情况下，非本地物种因其文化生态系统服务而迅速受到重视。

result.sourceSentence: For example, citizen groups have lobbied for the protection of non-native Eucalyptus trees in California and non-native dingos in Australia.
result.translation: 例如，公民团体曾游说保护加利福尼亚州的非本地桉树和澳大利亚的非本地澳洲野犬。

result.sourceSentence: The potentially positive contributions of non-native species to biodiversity and to the long-term welfare of humans are missing from current biodiversity indicators.
result.translation: 非本地物种对生物多样性以及人类长期福祉的潜在积极贡献，在当前的生物多样性指标中缺失。

result.sourceSentence: This raises the following questions: Are non-native species part of ‘nature’ or ‘biodiversity’ that we wish to preserve?
result.translation: 这就引出了以下问题：非本地物种是否属于我们希望保护的“自然”或“生物多样性”的一部分？

result.sourceSentence: If so, can they be integrated into a conservation planning process in a way that recognises their potential for undesirable effects but also captures their potential positive contributions to biodiversity and society?
result.translation: 如果是这样，它们能否被纳入保护规划过程，既认识到其潜在的不良影响，同时也涵盖它们对生物多样性和社会的潜在积极贡献？

result.sourceSentence: Biodiversity is a complex notion and the indicators that are used to track it are a reflection of available information, objectives, and values, which all can vary culturally and with time.
result.translation: 生物多样性是一个复杂的概念，用来追踪它的指标反映了现有信息、目标和价值观，而这些都可能随文化和时间而变化。

result.sourceSentence: However, it is important to ask under what circumstances it might be scientifically and politically desirable to modify some biodiversity indicators to include all species in light of ongoing preparations for the Post-2020 Strategic Plan of CBD, ongoing assessments by the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), and forthcoming national implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
result.translation: 然而，鉴于CBD“2020年后战略计划”正在进行的筹备工作、生物多样性和生态系统服务政府间科学政策平台（IPBES）正在开展的评估，以及各国即将推进的可持续发展目标（SDGs）实施工作，探讨在何种情况下修改部分生物多样性指标以纳入所有物种在科学和政治上可能是可取的，这一点十分重要。

result.sourceSentence: Non-native species as an integral component of biodiversity
result.translation: 非本地物种作为生物多样性不可或缺的组成部分

result.sourceSentence: There are several reasons why non-native species should be considered part of biodiversity and included in biodiversity and sustainability indices.
result.translation: 有几个原因说明为什么非本地物种应被视为生物多样性的一部分，并被纳入生物多样性和可持续性指数。

result.sourceSentence: First, the absence of non-native species from biodiversity indices stands in contradiction to the CBD and SDGs.
result.translation: 首先，生物多样性指数中缺少非本地物种，这与CBD和SDGs相矛盾。

result.sourceSentence: The CBD definition of biodiversity (Article 2) encompasses the biological dimensions of the world (genes, species, ecosystems and their interactions), but it makes no distinction between native and non-native life forms, nor does it refer to notions of ‘intactness’, which forms the basis for excluding non-native species from the Biodiversity Intactness Index.
result.translation: 《生物多样性公约》（第2条）对生物多样性的定义涵盖了世界的生物学维度（基因、物种、生态系统及其相互作用），但它并未区分本土与非本土生命形式，也未提及“完整性”概念，而这正是将非本土物种排除在生物多样性完整性指数之外的依据。

result.sourceSentence: Aichi Target 2 and Goal 15.9 of the SDGs require national and local governments to account for ‘the diverse values of biodiversity’.
result.translation: 爱知目标2和可持续发展目标15.9要求国家和地方政府考虑“生物多样性的多元价值”。

result.sourceSentence: Second, non-native species should be included in key biodiversity indices because they represent large fractions of modern ecosystems and regional species-pools.
result.translation: 其次，非本土物种应当被纳入关键生物多样性指数中，因为它们在现代生态系统和区域物种库中占很大比例。

result.sourceSentence: Non-native plants and birds can make up 50% or more of species in some urban, insular, and old-field environments.
result.translation: 在一些城市、岛屿和弃耕地环境中，非本土植物和鸟类可占物种的50%或以上。

result.sourceSentence: There is a risk that regional policy makers in areas in which non-native species comprise a significant component of the landscape will perceive biodiversity indices to be irrelevant if they are based solely on native species.
result.translation: 存在这样一种风险：在非本土物种构成景观重要组成部分的地区，如果生物多样性指数仅基于本土物种，区域政策制定者就会认为这些指数毫不相关。

result.sourceSentence: Finally, and perhaps most importantly, society’s motivations for the conservation of biodiversity are evolving and the indicators used to measure the state of the environment and progress towards our goals should too.
result.translation: 最后，或许也是最重要的一点，社会保护生物多样性的动机正在演变，用于衡量环境状况及迈向我们目标进展的指标也应当如此。

result.sourceSentence: Biodiversity indices will need to encompass all species if they are to remain socially relevant and illustrate the full gamut of what are now called ecosystem services (and disservices), or nature’s contributions to people.
result.translation: 如果生物多样性指数要保持社会相关性，并展现如今所谓的生态系统服务（与负服务）或自然对人类贡献的全貌，它们就需要涵盖所有物种。

result.sourceSentence: Drawbacks of accounting for non-native species
result.translation: 计入非本土物种的弊端

result.sourceSentence: Some will argue that if non-native species are considered as an integral part of biodiversity then, by extension, it will be harder to make the case that non-native species are potentially problematic.
result.translation: 有人会认为，如果将非本土物种视为生物多样性不可或缺的组成部分，那么推而广之，就更难论证非本土物种可能存在问题。

result.sourceSentence: Such a change might also be viewed as devaluing conservation efforts that focus on native species.
result.translation: 这种变化也可能被视为贬低了专注于本土物种的保护工作。

result.sourceSentence: Others have argued that some fraction of the negative impacts of non-native species may be underestimated and will only be known with time.
result.translation: 另一些人认为，非本土物种的部分负面影响可能被低估了，而且只有随着时间推移才会为人所知。

result.sourceSentence: These are legitimate concerns.
result.translation: 这些都是合理的担忧。

result.sourceSentence: Accounting for non-native species does not imply that they are inherently desirable, nor that native and non-native species are biologically or culturally interchangeable.
result.translation: 计入非本土物种并不意味着它们本质上是可取的，也不意味着本土与非本土物种在生物学或文化上可以互换。

result.sourceSentence: Nor does counting all species as an initial step to describing the environment preclude scientists from conducting risk assessments of different species or groups of species regarding undesirable outcomes.
result.translation: 将统计所有物种作为描述环境的初步步骤，也并不妨碍科学家针对不良后果对不同物种或物种群体进行风险评估。

result.sourceSentence: But to exclude non-native species a priori and without justification from indices and assessments of the state of the environment, as is sometimes done, prevents any subsequent debate about their relative merits.
result.translation: 然而，像有时那样先验地、毫无依据地将非本地物种排除在环境状况指数和评估之外，会阻碍后续对其相对优劣的讨论。

result.sourceSentence: Moving forward
result.translation: 展望未来

result.sourceSentence: There are several steps that can be taken to better align future conservation planning with the mission of CBD and the SDGs.
result.translation: 可以采取几项措施，使未来的保护规划更好地契合CBD和SDGs的使命。

result.sourceSentence: •	Data used for biodiversity assessments and conservation planning should, initially, include all species.
result.translation: •	用于生物多样性评估和保护规划的数据最初应包含所有物种。

result.sourceSentence: This will not only ensure that indices are representative of the environments they seek to characterise, but it will also align species richness and identity information with the functional information that is increasingly being measured remotely.
result.translation: 这不仅能确保指数代表其试图刻画的环境，而且还能使物种丰富度和身份信息与日益以远程方式测量的功能信息保持一致。

result.sourceSentence: •	Researchers should continue to investigate the extent to which non-native species influence the flow of ecosystem services and contribute to human well-being.
result.translation: •	研究人员应继续探究非本地物种在多大程度上影响生态系统服务的流动并增进人类福祉。

result.sourceSentence: One overlooked area of research is how including non-native species may alter existing biodiversity indices.
result.translation: 一个被忽视的研究领域是，纳入非本地物种可能会如何改变现有的生物多样性指数。

result.sourceSentence: Including non-native species into the Biodiversity Intactness Index can lead to a 10% improvement in the index score, and consideration of non-native populations in International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) protocols will reduce a species’ global risk of extinction.
result.translation: 将非本地物种纳入生物多样性完整度指数可使指数得分提高10%，而在世界自然保护联盟（IUCN）规程中考虑非本地种群将降低物种的全球灭绝风险。

result.sourceSentence: These examples hint that some existing index scores may be overly negative.
result.translation: 这些例子暗示，一些现有的指数得分可能过于负面。

result.sourceSentence: •	Panels that decide which indicators to use when assessing progress towards global conservation goals, especially those that establish a link with human well-being (e.g., Aichi Targets), should be composed of specialists and laypersons from a range of backgrounds.
result.translation: • 决定在评估实现全球保护目标的进展时使用哪些指标的小组——尤其是那些与人类福祉建立联系的目标（例如爱知目标）——应由来自多种背景的专家和非专业人士组成。

result.sourceSentence: Some indicators should reflect the preference of certain stakeholders for notions of ‘nativeness’ or ‘pristineness’, while others should capture all species found in modern ecosystems and their contributions to human well-being.
result.translation: 一些指标应反映特定利益相关者对“本地性”或“原始性”概念的偏好，而另一些则应涵盖现代生态系统中存在的所有物种及其对人类福祉的贡献。

result.sourceSentence: •	Biodiversity and sustainability assessments that exclude non-native species should systematically specify that they are tracking ‘native biodiversity’ and not ‘biodiversity’, as these terms are not synonymous.
result.translation: • 排除非本地物种的生物多样性与可持续性评估应系统地明确说明其追踪的是“本地生物多样性”而非“生物多样性”，因为这两个术语并非同义词。

result.sourceSentence: The idea of considering non-native species in biodiversity assessments remains controversial in part because it runs against decades of studies alerting policy makers and the public to the potential dangers associated with these species.
result.translation: 在生物多样性评估中考虑非本地物种的想法仍然有争议，部分原因是这有悖于数十年来警示政策制定者和公众注意与这些物种相关的潜在危险的研究。

result.sourceSentence: Scientifically and politically, however, it may be the best thing to do, as it will ultimately ensure that indices and the databases that underlie them cover all dimensions of the living world and remain relevant to groups of stakeholders that extend beyond conservation biologists.
result.translation: 然而，从科学和政治角度来看，这或许是最好的做法，因为这将最终确保各项指数及支撑它们的数据库涵盖生物世界的所有维度，并对保护生物学家之外的利益相关者群体保持相关性。

result.sourceSentence: The discussion about how to best integrate non-native species into biodiversity indicators will need to take place not only within a scientific debate about the contributions of these species to society but also a broader social debate about what type of nature we need to ensure a good life for present and future generations.
result.translation: 关于如何最好地将非本土物种纳入生物多样性指标的讨论，不仅需要在探讨这些物种对社会贡献的科学辩论中展开，也需要在关乎我们需要何种自然以保障当今和未来几代人美好生活的更广泛社会辩论中进行。

result.sourceSentence: Edited for reading; links, citations and media omitted.
result.translation: 为便于阅读而编辑；链接、引文和媒体均已省略。

result.sourceSentence: While it is recognized that language can pose a barrier to the transfer of scientific knowledge, the convergence on English as the global language of science may suggest that this problem has been resolved.
result.translation: 尽管人们认识到语言可能会对科学知识的传播构成障碍，但以英语作为全球科学语言的趋同趋势或许表明这一问题已经得到解决。

result.sourceSentence: However, our survey searching Google Scholar in 16 languages revealed that 35.6% of 75,513 scientific documents on biodiversity conservation published in 2014 were not in English.
result.translation: 然而，我们用16种语言检索谷歌学术的调查显示，2014年发表的75,513篇关于生物多样性保护的科学文献中，有35.6%并非英文。

result.sourceSentence: Ignoring such non-English knowledge can cause biases in our understanding of study systems.
result.translation: 忽视这类非英语知识可能会导致我们对研究系统的理解产生偏差。

result.sourceSentence: Furthermore, as publication in English has become prevalent, scientific knowledge is often unavailable in local languages.
result.translation: 此外，随着以英语发表变得普遍，科学知识往往无法以当地语言获取。

result.sourceSentence: This hinders its use by field practitioners and policy makers for local environmental issues; 54% of protected area directors in Spain identified languages as a barrier.
result.translation: 这阻碍了实地从业者和政策制定者在当地环境问题中使用这些知识；西班牙54%的保护区主管将语言视为障碍。

result.sourceSentence: We urge scientific communities to make a more concerted effort to tackle this problem and propose potential approaches both for compiling non-English scientific knowledge effectively and for enhancing the multilingualization of new and existing knowledge available only in English for the users of such knowledge.
result.translation: 我们敦促科学界做出更加协调一致的努力来应对这一问题，并提出潜在途径，既用于有效汇编非英语科学知识，也用于为这类知识的使用者加强仅以英语提供的新的和现有知识的多语言化。

result.sourceSentence: English is obviously the language that currently dominates global scientific activities as a lingua franca.
result.translation: 英语显然是目前作为通用语主导全球科学活动的语言。

result.sourceSentence: Locally, however, many scientists and users of scientific information, such as policy makers, communicate on a daily basis in languages other than English, which inevitably creates barriers to the transfer of knowledge between communities.
result.translation: 然而，在当地，许多科学家以及政策制定者等科学信息的使用者，日常都使用英语以外的语言进行交流，这不可避免地给不同群体之间的知识传递造成了障碍。

result.sourceSentence: However, the magnitude of this problem is not well quantified, and the consequences and solutions deserve further exploration.
result.translation: 然而，这一问题的规模尚未得到充分量化，其后果与解决方案也值得进一步探讨。

result.sourceSentence: Language barriers may be a particularly serious problem in subjects in which local knowledge is especially important, such as environmental sciences required for biodiversity conservation.
result.translation: 在本地知识尤为重要的学科中，例如生物多样性保护所需的环境科学，语言障碍可能是一个特别严重的问题。

result.sourceSentence: Languages can seriously limit the transfer of knowledge in environmental sciences in two directions: when compiling scientific knowledge—for example, in global assessments, such as those by the Intergovernmental Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES)—and when applying knowledge to local environmental issues, often tackled by field practitioners and local policy makers.
result.translation: 语言会在两个方向上严重限制环境科学中的知识传递：一是在汇编科学知识时——例如在政府间生物多样性和生态系统服务平台（IPBES）等进行的全球评估中；二是在将知识应用于当地环境问题时，而这些问题通常由一线从业人员和地方政策制定者应对。

result.sourceSentence: Focusing on environmental sciences as an example, we here investigate the potential extent and consequences of language barriers in the two directions and propose solutions for reducing this potentially overlooked problem.
result.translation: 我们在此以环境科学为例，研究语言障碍在这两个方向上的潜在范围与后果，并提出减轻这一可能被忽视的问题的解决方案。

result.sourceSentence: Language barriers can cause gaps in information availability during the global compilation of scientific knowledge, as scientific information is available not only in English but also in many other languages.
result.translation: 在全球汇编科学知识的过程中，语言障碍会造成信息获取上的缺口，因为科学信息不仅可通过英语获取，也可通过许多其他语言获取。

result.sourceSentence: We tried to estimate the number of conservation-related scientific documents published in the world’s major languages.
result.translation: 我们尝试估算以世界主要语言发表的与保护相关的科学文献数量。

result.sourceSentence: Searching for scientific documents published in 2014 with two keywords, “biodiversity” and “conservation”, in 16 languages on Google Scholar generated 75,513 manuscripts, of which English was by far the most frequently used language (48,600 scientific documents, 64.4%), followed by Spanish (9,520), Portuguese (7,800), simplified Chinese (4,540), and French (2,290).
result.translation: 在谷歌学术上以16种语言使用“生物多样性”和“保护”两个关键词检索2014年发表的科学文献，共获得75,513篇文稿，其中英语是迄今为止使用最频繁的语言（48,600篇科学文献，占64.4%），其次是西班牙语（9,520篇）、葡萄牙语（7,800篇）、简体中文（4,540篇）和法语（2,290篇）。

result.sourceSentence: The other 11 languages surveyed were used in a total of 2,763 documents (see for more detail).
result.translation: 所调查的其余11种语言共计用于2,763篇文献（参见更多详情）。

result.sourceSentence: By further investigating 95 sample documents from those obtained using Spanish terms (the sample size was validated by the “sample.size.prop” function in R package “samplingbook”, assuming the expected proportion was P = 0.48 [i.e., the actual proportion of Spanish-only documents], a finite small population correction of N = 9,520, precision e = 0.1, and confidence level = 0.95), we confirmed that all but one document was indeed written in Spanish.
result.translation: 通过进一步核查从西班牙语检索词所得结果中抽取的95篇样本文献（样本量由R语言软件包“samplingbook”中的“sample.size.prop”函数验证，假设预期比例P = 0.48［即纯西班牙语文献的实际比例］，有限小总体校正值N = 9,520，精度e = 0.1，置信水平= 0.95），我们确认除一篇文献外，其余均确实以西班牙语撰写。

result.sourceSentence: Furthermore, 46 (48% of the 95) of these documents provided neither the title nor the abstract in English.
result.translation: 此外，这些文献中有46篇（占这95篇的48%）既未提供英文标题，也未提供英文摘要。

result.sourceSentence: The result was similar when we investigated 80 sample documents from those obtained using Japanese terms (the sample size was determined in the same way but with N = 474); 35% of those documents provided neither the title nor the abstract in English.
result.translation: 当我们核查从日语检索词所得结果中抽取的80篇样本文献时，结果也类似（样本量以相同方式确定，但N = 474）；这些文献中有35%既未提供英文标题，也未提供英文摘要。

result.sourceSentence: Assuming similar proportions apply to other languages, these results suggest: (1) most of the 35.6% scientific documents written in a non-English language cannot be understood fully without the relevant non-English language skills, and (2) up to half of the non-English scientific documents are, in theory, unsearchable using English keywords.
result.translation: 假设类似比例也适用于其他语言，这些结果表明：（1）在以非英语语言撰写的35.6%的科学文献中，如果不具备相关的非英语语言能力，大多数文献无法被充分理解；（2）从理论上讲，多达一半的非英语科学文献无法使用英文关键词检索。

result.sourceSentence: Moreover, having English titles and abstracts may not suffice; of the 6 peer-reviewed papers published in Japanese by the first author of this paper (all with an English title and 3 also with an English abstract), 4 were not searchable using their English titles on Google Scholar, nor were two searchable on Web of Science.
result.translation: 此外，具备英文标题和摘要可能并不足够；在本文第一作者以日语发表的6篇同行评审论文中（均附有英文标题，其中3篇还附有英文摘要），有4篇无法在谷歌学术上通过其英文标题检索到，另有两篇也无法在Web of Science上检索到。

result.sourceSentence: All 6, however, appeared on Google Scholar when searched using their Japanese titles.
result.translation: 然而，当使用其日语标题检索时，这6篇全部出现在谷歌学术上。

result.sourceSentence: Google Scholar searches can include “grey literature” (usually not peer-reviewed).
result.translation: 谷歌学术检索可以包含“灰色文献”（通常未经同行评审）。

result.sourceSentence: However, of the 46 Spanish documents with neither an English title nor an English abstract, over half (26) were journal articles, books, or theses and thus are expected to have scientific credibility.
result.translation: 然而，在既没有英文标题也没有英文摘要的46篇西班牙语文献中，超过一半（26篇）是期刊文章、书籍或学位论文，因此预计具有科学可信度。

result.sourceSentence: Similarly, 43% (12) of the 28 Japanese documents with neither an English title nor an English abstract were journal articles.
result.translation: 同样，在既没有英文标题也没有英文摘要的28篇日语文献中，43%（12篇）是期刊文章。

result.sourceSentence: This proportion was higher in those documents with an English title and/or an English abstract in both languages.
result.translation: 在这两种语言中，带有英文标题和/或英文摘要的文献里，这一比例更高。

result.sourceSentence: While some of these non-English journals might not necessarily be committed to publishing papers of reasonable quality, there are also well-established journals that regularly publish a non-negligible number of peer-reviewed papers on biodiversity conservation in non-English languages (see examples in ).
result.translation: 虽然其中一些非英语期刊可能未必致力于发表质量尚可的论文，但也有成熟的期刊定期以非英语语言发表数量不容忽视的关于生物多样性保护的同行评审论文（参见示例）。

result.sourceSentence: The same is true for scientific data: global (i.e., English-based) biodiversity databases store fewer data from countries with fewer English speakers, but this could be partly because data from those countries are not necessarily available in English.
result.translation: 科学数据同样如此：全球（即基于英语的）生物多样性数据库所存储的来自英语使用者较少的国家的数据较少，但这可能部分是因为这些国家的数据未必以英语提供。

result.sourceSentence: For example, over 4 million records on species occurrence and abundance, including over 1 million based on monitoring surveys organized by the Ministry of the Environment in Japan, are available online ( but currently only in Japanese.
result.translation: 例如，超过400万条关于物种分布和丰度的记录（其中包括超过100万条基于日本环境省组织的监测调查）均可在网上获取，但目前仅有日语版本。

result.sourceSentence: In fact, the consequences of ignoring non-English science may be more serious than merely lacking access to 36% of existing information; it can cause biases and gaps in our understanding of the global environment.
result.translation: 事实上，忽视非英语科学的后果可能比仅仅无法获取36%的现有信息更为严重；它会导致我们对全球环境的理解出现偏差和空白。

result.sourceSentence: One potential bias in systematic reviews of English-language journals is the over-representation of positive and/or statistically significant results, as they are more likely to be published in high-impact English journals.
result.translation: 英文期刊系统综述中的一个潜在偏倚是阳性和/或具有统计学意义的结果占比过高，因为它们更有可能发表在高影响力的英文期刊上。

result.sourceSentence: Another type of bias, of particular relevance to environmental sciences, is that information on species, habitats, ecosystems, and phenomena that are specific to countries where English is not the mother tongue can be overlooked when searched only in English, as also reported in medical sciences.
result.translation: 另一种与环境科学尤为相关的偏倚是：当仅用英语检索时，英语并非母语的国家所特有的物种、栖息地、生态系统和现象的相关信息可能会被忽视，这一点在医学科学中也曾有报道。

result.sourceSentence: As an example, the latest estimates of population status in Taiwan for fairy pittas (Pitta nympha), a bird species of conservation concern, are available only in traditional Chinese ( and not used in the global assessment by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (Chie-Jen Ko, personal communications).
result.translation: 例如，受保护关注的鸟类物种仙八色鸫（Pitta nympha）在台湾种群状况的最新估算仅以繁体中文提供，且未用于世界自然保护联盟的全球评估（Chie-Jen Ko，个人通信）。

result.sourceSentence: Similarly, important papers reporting the infection of pigs with avian influenza viruses in China initially went unnoticed by international communities, including the World Health Organization and the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, because they were published in Chinese-language journals.
result.translation: 同样，报道中国猪只感染禽流感病毒的重要论文起初未引起包括世界卫生组织和联合国粮食及农业组织在内的国际社会的注意，因为它们发表在中文期刊上。

result.sourceSentence: Also, there is a recognized knowledge gap about the effects on biodiversity of some crops, such as soybeans, sorghum, and cotton, but considering that these crops are grown over large areas in South America and China, scientific literature on these crops may exist in the local languages of these regions.
result.translation: 此外，关于大豆、高粱和棉花等部分作物对生物多样性的影响，存在公认的知识空白；但考虑到这些作物在南美洲和中国大面积种植，关于这些作物的科学文献可能以这些地区的当地语言存在。

result.sourceSentence: Finally, scientific knowledge generated by those undertaking conservation activities in the field (field practitioners) could also be under-represented in English, as field practitioners often find it a challenge to have their work published in academic journals, particularly in English if they are non-native English speakers.
result.translation: 最后，由在野外开展保护活动的人员（一线实践者）产生的科学知识，在英语中也可能代表性不足，因为一线实践者往往觉得将自己的工作发表在学术期刊上颇具挑战，尤其是如果他们是非英语母语者，要用英语发表就更是如此。

result.sourceSentence: This potentially renders local and indigenous knowledge unavailable in English.
result.translation: 这可能会使本地和原住民知识在英语中无法获取。

result.sourceSentence: For example, Wetlands International Argentina has produced over 20 technical publications on the conservation and management of wetlands over the past 20 years, but only 2 are available in English (Daniel E. Blanco, personal communications).
result.translation: 例如，湿地国际阿根廷分部在过去20年间推出了超过20份关于湿地保护与管理的技术出版物，但只有2份有英文版（丹尼尔·E·布兰科，个人通信）。

result.sourceSentence: Their non-English publications include a report on the roles of peatlands, a wetland type of potential global importance, in mitigating climate change impacts ( Such knowledge generated by practitioners is often overlooked as grey literature but forms a vital part of the evidence base.
result.translation: 他们的非英文出版物包括一份关于泥炭地（一种具有潜在全球重要性的湿地类型）在缓解气候变化影响方面所起作用的报告。这类由实践者产生的知识往往被视为灰色文献而遭忽视，但却是证据基础中至关重要的组成部分。

result.sourceSentence: For instance, the IPBES has recently shown that local and indigenous knowledge is a key to understanding the conservation of ecosystem services by pollinators (
result.translation: 例如，IPBES最近表明，本地和原住民知识是理解传粉者生态系统服务保护的关键。

result.sourceSentence: Another consequence of language barriers that is becoming increasingly important operates in the opposite direction: much scientific knowledge is now unavailable in local languages, as publication in English has become prevalent.
result.translation: 语言障碍的另一个日益重要的后果表现在相反方向：由于用英语发表已变得普遍，如今大量科学知识在当地语言中无法获取。

result.sourceSentence: A factor behind this is that even scientists whose mother tongue is not English aim to produce papers in English for publication in high-impact journals given the clear advantages for their careers.
result.translation: 这背后的一个因素是，考虑到这对他们职业发展的明显优势，即使是母语非英语的科学家也力求用英语撰写论文，以便在高影响力期刊上发表。

result.sourceSentence: Furthermore, many journals, previously published in local languages, are now publishing mainly in English to increase their impacts on scientific communities globally (e.g., Animal Biodiversity and Conservation in Spain, Natureza & Conservação in Brazil).
result.translation: 此外，许多此前以当地语言出版的期刊如今主要用英语出版，以提高其对全球科学界的影响力（例如西班牙的《Animal Biodiversity and Conservation》、巴西的《Natureza & Conservação》）。

result.sourceSentence: As a consequence, there exists an imbalance in knowledge transfer in countries where English is not the mother tongue; much scientific knowledge that has originated there and elsewhere is available only in English and not in their local languages.
result.translation: 因此，在英语并非母语的国家，知识传播存在失衡；大量源自当地及其他地区的科学知识仅以英语提供，而不是以当地语言提供。
